statusText: Roughly four hours into the U.S. cash session, the Nasdaq-100 complex holds its advance after the S&P 500 briefly set a fresh record above 7,800 (7,816.70) before pulling back to roughly 7,784 -- an observed, orderly retracement rather than a failed one. QQQ was last quoted near 730.28, up about 1.05% versus Wednesday's 723.70 close, inside today's 724.04-733.76 range and modestly off the session high. A flat July PPI print released this morning reinforced yesterday's benign CPI and added to Fed-hold/cut bets, with the 10-year Treasury yield easing toward roughly 4.68%. VIX remains compressed near 14.45, its lowest close since January. Cisco fell sharply despite beating estimates -- an idiosyncratic single-name reaction, not a systemic signal -- while Applied Materials still reports after today's close (call ~20:30 UTC). Tail stays low with no observed failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure; the confirmed S&P/QQQ retracement from intraday highs argues against extension risk. Stress eases modestly as today's PPI catalyst has now printed and resolved calmly, though it stays in the moderate zone on the unresolved Hormuz standoff (traffic near three-month lows, no new escalation) and the pending Applied Materials print.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Reassess as the session either extends today's gain into the close or fades, and again around Applied Materials' after-close earnings call (~20:30 UTC) and tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print; an upgrade to a higher Tail state requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks, not the pending catalysts themselves.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its midday advance -- QQQ near +1% off a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 -- as a flat July PPI reinforces cooling inflation and VIX sits near a seven-month low; Tail stays low while Stress eases on a confirmed intraday pullback ahead of tonight's Applied Materials earnings
body: Roughly four hours after the 13:30 UTC cash open, web reporting confirms the Nasdaq-100 complex extends its advance: Invesco QQQ Trust was last quoted at 730.28, up about 1.05% versus Wednesday's 723.70 close, trading inside today's 724.04-733.76 range and modestly below the session high. The S&P 500 briefly cleared 7,800 for the first time, setting a fresh record at 7,816.70, before retracing to roughly 7,784 -- a confirmed, orderly pullback rather than a failed one, which argues against extension risk rather than for it. A flat July producer price index, released this morning, reinforced yesterday's benign CPI print and gave traders a fresh reason to buy, with the 10-year Treasury yield easing further to roughly 4.68% (Wednesday's close) on reinforced Fed-hold/cut bets; Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD feed still returns Aug 11 prints (10Y 4.70%, 2Y 4.22%), now five sessions stale. NQ futures search results again returned the identical 29,805.75 last / 29,712.25 open / 29,668.25-30,001.75 range figures seen in each of the last four hourly checks -- now five consecutive identical reads -- confirming this is a stale, cached snapshot rather than live structure; it is excluded from the current price-path assessment and QQQ's intraday move is used as the primary proxy instead. VIX was last reported near 14.45, its lowest close since January, consistent with continued volatility compression. Alpha Vantage's GLOBAL_QUOTE call returned an explicit daily rate_limit error this run (25-request/day free-tier cap exhausted, confirmed again on retry after a 15-second wait), so MARKET_STATUS, WTI and NEWS_SENTIMENT were not attempted this run to avoid wasting budget; U.S. cash-session status (13:30-20:00 UTC, currently open) is inferred from the current clock time and corroborating web reporting instead. Cisco fell sharply (reported down over 6%) despite beating earnings estimates -- an idiosyncratic single-name reaction to guidance/valuation, not a systemic signal, and QQQ's continued advance confirms it has not spread. Applied Materials still reports fiscal Q3 earnings after today's close with its call at 20:30 UTC; the stock traded higher into the print on AI-chip and advanced-packaging demand optimism. Iran's Hormuz standoff remains unresolved -- CNBC reports strait traffic near three-month lows and Tehran disputing Trump's 'total control' claim -- with no new escalatory shock or transmission event identified since the prior run. Given the confirmed intraday pullback from both the S&P and QQQ session highs, and no failed-retracement or repeated-extension structure, Tail eases slightly to 15% (from 16%), still low. Stress eases to 32% as today's PPI catalyst has now printed and resolved calmly and VIX stays compressed, moving further into the lower half of the moderate zone while the unresolved Hormuz backdrop and pending AMAT print keep it out of the low band. Confidence improves modestly to 54%, reflecting a fresher, more specific QQQ intraday quote and confirmed S&P record/pullback levels from web reporting, offset by Alpha Vantage's Treasury data now five sessions stale, an exhausted daily Alpha Vantage budget after only two successful calls this run, and NQ futures data confirmed stale across five consecutive hourly checks.

forecastDetail.comment: Roughly four hours into the cash session, the confirmed QQQ/S&P pullback from intraday highs argues against extension risk; Stress eases as today's PPI print has already resolved calmly and VIX stays compressed near 14.5.

Approaching the mid-to-late afternoon, Stress ticks up modestly as the market moves toward the 20:00 UTC close and tonight's Applied Materials earnings call, though no failed-pullback structure is observed yet.
Stress builds further into the final trading hour as positioning ahead of the AMAT print and the cash close typically thins liquidity; Tail stays low absent observed one-way continuation.

The 20:00 UTC cash close coincides with Applied Materials' earnings call at 20:30 UTC; Stress peaks for the day on the event/whipsaw risk of an earnings-driven semiconductor-equipment reaction, though pre-event alignment is not treated as already observed.
The AMAT after-hours reaction continues to resolve; Stress stays elevated within the moderate band until the initial post-earnings move is confirmed one way or the other.
As the post-earnings reaction settles into the evening, Stress eases back toward the day's lower range with no confirmed failed-retracement structure carried into the close.
